# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can touch only the action controls, and currently have no reliable information about the wires or the manual’s required condition. I’m asking Mute to provide the manual rule and to relay the Deaf’s visual observations before any cut is attempted.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please read the manual rule exactly and obtain the Deaf's complete observations of the display, light, plate marking, and wire colours or markings. Relay all relevant information to me before any action.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf sees display 0. Light off. Plate engraved question mark. Wires in order: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.

The Deaf reports display 0, light off, a question-mark plate, and wire colours in order: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. I still lack the manual rule, so cutting any wire would be unsafe. I’m requesting the manual’s exact instruction and confirmation of these observations.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received: display 0, light off, plate question mark, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. What exact rule does the manual give for this configuration? Do not instruct a cut until you have checked it.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible state unchanged: display 0, light off, plate engraved question mark, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.

The visual state is unchanged, and the manual rule is still missing. No wire can safely be selected from the available information, so I am again requesting the manual instruction from Mute.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The Deaf confirms the same state: display 0, light off, plate question mark, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Please send the exact manual rule now; I will not cut without it.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signaled: thumbs down, then pointing at you, then pointing right. No bomb change: display 0, light off, plate question mark, wires yellow green red.

The new gestures appear to be a nonverbal instruction from Mute directed at me, but they do not unambiguously identify a wire position. Since I cannot see gestures, I need Mute to state the required wire number in spoken words. No cut is safe yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received the report of your gestures, but I cannot interpret them reliably. Please speak the required wire position explicitly as a number: cut 1, cut 2, or cut 3. Confirm the manual rule first.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No bomb change: display 0, light off, plate question mark, wires 1 yellow 2 green 3 red. Mute gestured: pointing at me, pointing right, handshake, thumbs down.

Mute’s reported gestures still do not establish a safe wire number: “pointing right” might indicate a position, but the handshake and thumbs-down make the intended instruction ambiguous. I will request a deliberately unambiguous one-wire signal, with confirmation, and wait for Deaf to report it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please signal exactly one wire: point left for wire 1, point straight/down for wire 2, or point right for wire 3, then give thumbs up to confirm. Deaf will relay your signal.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 0, light off, plate question mark, wires 1 yellow 2 green 3 red. Mute gestured pointing at me, thumbs down, pointing right; meaning unknown.

Mute cannot speak, so my earlier request for spoken confirmation was impossible. The gestures reported so far are ambiguous because several were combined. I will establish a one-gesture code: left means wire 1, up means wire 2, and right means wire 3. Mute should send exactly one of those, with no confirmation gesture.

```text
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👈"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👈"])
speak(to="mute", text="Send exactly one gesture in your next turn: 👈 means cut wire 1, ☝ means cut wire 2, 👉 means cut wire 3. Send no other gesture. Deaf should report it.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see your gesture pointing left. Bomb unchanged: display 0, light off, plate question mark, wires 1 yellow 2 green 3 red. I do not know what left denotes.

My left-pointing gesture was only a proposed code, not evidence about the correct wire. The manual’s rule remains unknown, so cutting any wire would still be unsafe. I’m asking Mute to provide the rule in a way that can reach me: spoken words are possible from Mute only on the next round, while gestures cannot convey their meaning to me directly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your manual rule is still essential. On your next turn, communicate the required wire by making exactly one gesture: 👈 for wire 1, ☝ for wire 2, or 👉 for wire 3. Deaf must report only which gesture you made, with no extra gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 0, light off, plate question mark, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Mute just signaled thumbs down; no actionable meaning is established.

The thumbs-down signal still does not identify a wire, and no manual rule has reached me. I will not risk a cut. I’m restating the code to Mute and asking Deaf to report the next single gesture exactly, without interpreting it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Do not use thumbs down. Make exactly one gesture next turn: 👈 means wire 1, ☝ means wire 2, 👉 means wire 3. Make no other gesture.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
speak(to="deaf", text="Please report exactly which single gesture Mute makes next, if any. Do not interpret it.")
wait()
```
